title: Reading +, −, and = symbols
keyIdea: The + sign means put together (add). The − sign means take away (subtract). The = sign means is the same as — both sides have the same value, not just “write the answer on the right”.
familyTip: Write 4 + 2 = 6 and 6 = 4 + 2 on a whiteboard. Ask your child to read both aloud and say why both are fair.

visual.caption: Choose + or −, change the numbers, and read the sentence. The bottom row shows what = means.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: name +, − and =, read a sentence aloud, catch the answer-box myth, then challenge.

kid: Equals (=) means is the same as.
Both sides of = must match in value.
adult: NC Y1 Number / CCSS 1.OA: read and interpret +, − and = in number sentences. Equals means sameness of value, not a cue to write an answer on the right.
Common mistakes: reading + as take-away; treating = as an answer box; rejecting sentences like 5 = 2 + 3.
In the lab your child names each sign, reads 3 + 2 = 5 in words, accepts 5 = 3 + 2 as fair, then tries the challenge.
